hypothesis.hypothesis:
Build the r11s1 front end (direct-mapped read-only I-cache, real F/D flop stage, ID/regfile/
hazard/forward reading F/D flops) but restructure it so that `hit` (tag compare) and the bus
`imem_ready` are never inputs of next_fpc or the fpc clock-enable. The fpc loop contains only
{fpc flop -> LUT-RAM hint read + BHT read -> kind/BHT decode -> 4:1 next_fpc mux -> fpc}, with
the CE being the existing hold (load-use / dmem / MDU, all early flop- or input-derived
signals). Everything that depends on `hit` ends at an F/D flop D pin and is verified one cycle
later from registered F/D flags.

1. rtl/icache.sv (new): 256 lines, direct-mapped, index = fpc[9:2], async-read distributed RAM
   (syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram", the style r8s0/r11s1 got through Gowin and formal). Line =
   {tag = fpc[19:10], 32-bit instruction, hint}. hint = {kind (none/jal/branch/ret), is_call,
   static target [20:2]} computed at FILL time from the raw bus word (imem_data -> predecode ->
   19-bit adder -> RAM write data, which ends at a RAM write port, not in the fetch loop).
   Static-target legality (word aligned, < 1 MiB, no wrap) is folded into kind=none at fill.
   Fill on every imem_ready miss at fpc (also while F/D is held, so a held fetch is refetched
   as a hit). Validity by a post-reset sweep that clears tag/valid one line per cycle while a
   registered `sweeping` flag forces hit = 0, forces the hint kind to `none` and suppresses
   fills (~256 cycles, long before the CoreMark start marker). No memory `initial` values
   (r8s1: smtbmc blow-up). Stores are not snooped; FENCE.I stays an architectural NOP.

2. rtl/if_stage.sv: IF/ID becomes a real F/D register {pc, instr, valid, pred_taken,
   pred_target, bht_cnt} plus private flags {fd_hit, fd_spec, fd_retry, kind/is_call}.
     hold   = load_use || dmem_stall || mdu_stall   (imem_ready NOT included)
     hit    = tag match && valid && !sweeping            (feeds F/D data flops only)
     opt_taken/opt_target = decode of the CACHED hint at fpc + bht_cnt[1] + ras0 (no hit term)
     next_fpc = kill ? kill_target
              : replay_now ? replay_pc
              : opt_taken ? opt_target : fpc + 4
     fpc <= next_fpc unless hold (kill and replay_now override hold, as kill does today)
     F/D <= { fpc,
              f_instr = hit ? c_instr : imem_data,       (RAM -> compare -> mux -> flop D)
              valid   = (hit || imem_ready) && !kill && !replay_now,
              pred_taken = hit && opt_taken, pred_target = opt_target, bht_cnt,
              fd_hit = hit,
              fd_spec = !hit && opt_taken,    // front end followed a garbage alias hint
              fd_retry = !hit && !imem_ready } // no instruction was delivered
     When valid=0 the F/D instruction is NOP 0x00000013 so decode of a bubble is benign.
   Replay (the one-stage-late verification, from F/D flops only):
     replay_now = !kill && (fd_retry || fd_spec) && !hold
     replay_pc  = fd_retry ? fd_pc : fd_pc + 4      (registered start point -> fpc D pin)
   i.e. a miss that got no bus word is refetched (one extra wasted cycle vs r11s1), and a miss
   whose next fetch followed an alias line's taken hint is repointed to pc+4 (no prediction on
   a miss, same as r11s1). A miss where the alias hint was `none` costs nothing extra (fpc+4
   was already right); a hit never pays. Expected extra cost vs r11s1: ~25% of misses (+retry
   of the ~22% no-bus misses), about +1-2% cycles. Mispredict recovery stays 3 cycles like
   r11s1 (kill flushes F/D, the ID/EX bubble as today).

3. rtl/branch_predictor.sv: the fetch-time predictor consumes the cached hint (kind, static
   target) and the BHT counter at fpc[8:2] with NO dependence on hit, so there is no adder and no
   opcode compare and no tag compare in the loop. RAS top (ras0) supplies the `ret` target.
   RAS push/pop and the BHT/EX-update stage are unchanged from the champion: RAS push/pop fire
   when the F/D load really happens (!hold, !kill, valid), using the F/D-registered
   kind/is_call (hit hint on a hit, predecode of the raw bus word on a miss), so they never
   see garbage alias hints and end at RAS flops only. A one-cycle-stale RAS only costs
   performance (EX checks every `ret`).

4. rtl/hazard_unit.sv, rtl/core.sv, rtl/id_stage.sv: regfile read addresses, load-use compare
   and forward-select inputs come from the F/D instruction flops (not io_imemData); imem_ready
   removed from stall_if / flush_if (the F/D valid flop carries bubbles); dmem_stall / kill /
   mdu precedence exactly as today; EX prediction check and kill_q recovery untouched; RVFI
   reporting unchanged. io_imemAddr stays the fpc flop (timed output).

Why this should work: (a) both measured quantities are known (r11s1 cycles 3.74M, +18.4%
iter/cycle; r11s1 Fmax limited by the fetch loop, not by the 16 ns ID cones the champion
already sits on), (b) `hit` now terminates at F/D flop D pins (RAM -> compare -> 2:1 mux), a
~6-level path, and at the RAS/F/D CEs, none of which feed fpc, (c) the fpc loop drops from 10
levels to roughly RAM read + decode + 4:1 mux, the same depth class as the champion's pc ->
predictor -> next_pc loop (which already runs ~16 ns including the imem_data predecode). Risks:
LUT count (~6.1K in r11s1, well under the 10K target), the ~10% place-and-route seed spread,
and the replay bookkeeping (formal exercises the all-miss path including retry/replay during
the sweep window, so it will catch protocol bugs). If the timing report still shows the RAM
read as the top startpoint, drop to 128 lines or shrink the tag to 8 bits (alias risk is only
a performance question because fetched instructions on a hit are always tag-verified; use
full pc[19:10] or leave as is if resources allow).

changes.description: New module. 256-line direct-mapped read-only I-cache in async-read distributed RAM, line = {tag, 32-bit instruction, fill-time predecode hint (kind, is_call, 19-bit static target)}. Hint computed from the raw bus word at fill time. Fill on imem_ready miss even while F/D is held. Reset sweep invalidation with a registered `sweeping` flag forcing hit=0 and kind=none and suppressing fills. No memory initial values. Outputs tag-match hit (consumed only by F/D data flops), cached instruction and cached hint for fpc.

Make IF/ID a real F/D flop stage with private flags (fd_hit, fd_spec, fd_retry, kind/is_call). next_fpc = kill ? kill_target : replay_now ? replay_pc : opt_taken ? opt_target : fpc+4 where opt_* come from the cached hint and BHT with no hit/imem_ready term; fpc CE = !hold only. F/D load uses hit and imem_ready (valid = (hit || imem_ready) && !kill && !replay_now, f_instr = hit ? cached : bus). One-stage-late replay from F/D flops: fd_retry -> refetch fd_pc, fd_spec -> fd_pc+4. Bubbles carry NOP instruction with valid=0.

Predict from the cached hint (kind + stored static target + BHT counter + RAS top) with no adder, opcode compare or tag compare in the fetch loop. pred_taken reported to EX is gated with hit at the F/D flop. RAS push/pop moved to the F/D load (fire = F/D advancing) using F/D-registered kind/is_call (hint on hit, raw-word predecode on miss). BHT storage and the registered EX update stage unchanged.

title: Line-embedded next-PC predictor in a registered-output I-cache: parallel hit/miss candidates, late hit select
motivation:
Every pure direction/indirect/recovery predictor is capped at ~1-2.5% of cycles
(mispredicts are ~110K of 4.43M cycles; r6s2/r7s2/r9s2/r10s2/r11s2 all landed inside
place-and-route noise or below), so the only predictor-side lever with real cycle
upside is the fetch-side one: a next-fetch-PC predictor that lives next to local
instruction storage and hides the ~22% imem backpressure.
r11s1 already measured that lever: a 256-line direct-mapped LUT-RAM I-cache whose output
is registered into a real F/D flop stage (hint predecoded at fill time) cut cycles
4,431,994 -> 3,737,708 (+18.6% iterations/cycle, formal and cosim clean) and scored
234.56 (+4.1%, just under the 4.6% bar) at Fmax 87.7 MHz (seeds 79.1/87.7/87.7), i.e. a
12% Fmax give-back against the 99.9 MHz champion. Its worst path was NOT an ID/EX cone:
cpu/u_if/fpc_5 -> cpu/u_if/fpc_18, 17.9 ns, 20 cells through u_ic -> u_if -> u_bp -> u_if.
That is the fetch loop itself: LUT-RAM read -> tag compare -> `hit` -> hint decode / hit
gating inside the predictor -> RAS/target/pc+4 mux -> next_fpc, all in series. The cycle
win is already banked; recovering even half of the Fmax give-back would clear the bar
(break-even for +4.6% is Fmax >= ~88 MHz at 3.74M cycles; at ~95 MHz the score is ~254).

title: One-hot AND-OR regfile read ports (kept decode lines) replace the 5-deep 2:1 mux chain
motivation:

shows the top paths are routing-dominated (~63% of the 11 ns data path is net
delay) and fall in two tied groups, both ending in the ID operand capture:
  (1) lfsr_24 (imem rs2-address bit) -> rs2_nxt_14_s11 (fanout 8) ->
      rs2_nxt_27_s25 (fanout 32, 3.03 ns net) -> a CHAIN of five LUT4s
      (rs2_nxt_2_s19 -> s13 -> s5 -> s1 -> s0) -> op_b_nxt -> op_b flop: 9 cells,
      16.313 ns arrival.
  (2) BSRAM DO -> u_mem wb_next (5 LUT levels) -> rs2_nxt -> op_b_nxt: 16.329 ns.

maps as a balanced tree of 2:1 mux LUT4s (5 levels, 31 LUT4 per bit per port, so

distributed RAM, banked, zero-gate, replicated select nets r12s0) only changed

read is both shallower (decode + 3 LUT4 levels: 16 x AND-OR2, 4 x OR4, 1 x OR4,
versus 5 mux levels) and smaller (21 LUT4 per bit per port instead of 31).

title: Tag-free fetch loop: line-index-speculative next-PC predictor in a registered-output I-cache, tag/hit verified one stage later
motivation:
Pure direction / indirect / recovery predictors are exhausted (r6s2, r7s2, r9s2, r10s2, r11s2: all
inside place-and-route noise; mispredicts are only ~110K of 4.43M cycles). The one predictor-side
lever with real cycle upside is the fetch-side next-PC predictor that sits next to local instruction
storage. r11s1 (experiments/log.jsonl, hyp-20261003-002-r11s1) measured it: a 256-line direct-mapped
LUT-RAM I-cache with a registered F/D flop stage and fill-time predecode hints cut cycles
4,431,994 -> 3,737,708 (+18.6% iterations/cycle, formal + cosim clean) and scored 234.56 (+4.10%,
just under the 4.6% bar) with Fmax 87.67 MHz (seeds 79.1 / 87.7 / 87.7) vs the champion's 99.87.
Its worst path (make timing, 17.94 ns, 20 cells, 10 levels) is the new fetch loop itself:
cpu/u_if/fpc_5 -> u_ic (LUT-RAM read + tag compare = hit) -> u_if (f_ok / hit gating) -> u_bp
(kind decode, RAS/target select) -> u_if (next_fpc mux + fpc CE) -> fpc_18. The ID cones are back
at the ~16 ns floor, so the cycle win is already banked and ~10-12% of Fmax is waiting in the loop.
Both r12 retries (r12s1 hit-free loop, r12s2 line-embedded next-PC) were never scored: they died
in run_all.sh at the 2700 s formal budget (causal_ch0 stuck in bitwuzla at step 2), i.e. an
infrastructure failure of the implementation, not a measured design failure.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Rebuild the r11s1 front end (read its full description in log.jsonl: direct-mapped read-only
I-cache, 256 lines, async-read distributed RAM, fill on imem_ready miss even while F/D is held,
fill-time predecode hint, reset sweep for validity with hit forced 0 and fills suppressed, real F/D
flop stage so regfile/hazard/forward read F/D flops, +1-cycle mispredict recovery) and change ONE
thing in the fpc loop: the tag compare, `hit` and `imem_ready` are removed from next_fpc and from
the fpc clock-enable. The loop becomes
    fpc flop -> {hint RAM read, BHT read (both indexed by fpc[9:2])}
             -> spec_taken = k_always | (k_br & bht_cnt[1]);  spec_tgt = k_ret ? ras0 : hint.tgt
             -> next_fpc = kill ? kill_target : fix ? fix_tgt : (spec_taken ? spec_tgt : fpc+1)
             -> fpc (CE = !hold, hold = load-use | dmem stall | MDU stall, all early flop/input terms)
i.e. RAM read + ~3 LUT levels, no 11-bit compare and no bus input. The fill-time hint is stored as
one-hot kind bits {k_always (JAL), k_br, k_ret}, is_call and the 18-bit static target, so no adder
or opcode compare is in the loop.
Everything that depends on `hit` ends at a flop D pin and is verified one cycle later from
REGISTERED flags (fd_hit_q, fd_spec_taken_q, fd_pc_q):
  - slot gets an instruction iff hit | imem_ready; otherwise F/D <= NOP/valid=0 and fd_replay_q is set.
  - replay (fd_replay_q): fpc <= fd_pc_q (the slot that failed) and the slot fetched this cycle is
    squashed to a bubble. A miss+stall now costs one extra cycle vs holding in place; it affects only
    ~6% misses x 22% stalls (~1.3% of fetch cycles).
  - alias fix (fd_spec_taken_q && !fd_hit_q): the hint read for a missing line belongs to another PC,
    so the speculative redirect is bogus. The slot itself is valid (it came from the bus), only the
    younger wrong-path fetch is squashed and fpc <= fd_pc_q + 1 (this is a miss: no prediction
    followed, same as r11s1). fix/replay share one `fd_redirect` flop-sourced select and one target
    adder fed only from registered fd_pc_q, so neither joins the kill/EX cone.
  - RAS push/pop and BHT read-counter capture are gated by the registered/late `hit` only at the RAS
    flop CE/D pins (endpoint, not loop); on a miss the predecode of the raw bus word drives push/pop
    as in r11s1. A bogus speculative RAS pop for an aliased miss is just a performance pollution
    (RAS has no repair today).
  - EX prediction check, kill_q recovery, BHT update stage: untouched. A speculative redirect that
    survives into ID/EX carries pred_taken/pred_target exactly as today, so EX still verifies it.
Formal-safety rules (the cause of both r12 failures; follow them strictly):
  1. Keep the memory structure identical to what r11s1 got through formal: flat async-read
     syn_ramstyle="distributed_ram" arrays, one write port, no `initial` values, no
     per-line valid flop vector (r8s1 / r12 timeouts); validity via the reset sweep.
  2. Add NO new memory array and no wider state than r11s1 plus ~40 flops (fd_pc_q, 3 flags).
  3. Before the full suite, run just `causal_ch0` and one `insn_*` check from formal/run_all.sh with a
     10 minute cap; if causal_ch0 sits at "Skipping step 1.." for minutes, shrink the cache to 128
     lines and/or drop the hint-target RAM column (recompute pc+imm in the F/D stage) rather than
     adding more logic.
  4. Do not use ifdef RISCV_FORMAL to remove the cache from the formal netlist.
Expected: cycles ~3.75-3.80M (+17-18% iter/cycle vs 4.43M, the replay costs ~1% over r11s1), loop
17.9 -> ~12-13 ns so Fmax is limited by the shared ~16 ns ID cones again, ~92-96 MHz median ->
score ~245-255 (+9-13% over the 225.33 champion); break-even for the 4.6% bar at 3.78M cycles is
Fmax >= ~89 MHz, i.e. only ~1.5 MHz above r11s1's measured 87.67. If the new critical path reappears
elsewhere in the loop (fpc+1 incrementer, ras0 -> target mux) say so in implementation_notes.md and
register fpc+1 as a shadow flop (fpc_plus1_q computed from next_fpc) as the first fallback.

title: Late-hit single-LUT F/D capture plus placement-decoupled regfile address flops (fd_rs1a/fd_rs2a)
motivation:
A fresh `make timing` of the r13s2 champion (place option 0, 77.4 MHz; the
91.75 MHz seeds are the same structure) shows two cones tied at ~18.1-18.2 ns
arrival, and both are dominated by routing/fan-out, not by logic:
(A) fpc_4 -> hint/tag RAM read (RAD net 1.98 ns, 16:1 read mux) -> 8-cell
carry-chain tag compare -> `hit`, then THREE serial LUTs with fan-out 36, 33
and 1 (n539 -> n536 -> n529, nets 1.59 + 1.23 + 1.74 ns) into fd_instr[*]/D.
Everything after the carry chain is 5.8 ns for what is logically a
4-input function per bit. (B) fd_instr_20 (fan-out 38, one 3.41 ns net to a
fan-out-32 regfile read decode LUT placed 27 columns away) -> 32:1 read mux
chain -> id_stage rs2_nxt -> reg_q.rs2_val: 9.1 of 12.5 ns is route. The F/D
instruction flops are pulled towards the I-cache on their D side and
towards the regfile on their Q side, so the same flop pays a long net on
both. Earlier cone rewrites lost because cutting only one of two tied cones
cannot move Fmax; this hypothesis uses the slack freed on cone A to pay
for decoupling cone B.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Two cycle-neutral, behaviour-neutral edits in the front end.
(1) F/D capture with `hit` entering only the last LUT. Precompute the
early alternative alt_instr = imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP (inputs/flops
only; mark it syn_keep so the mapper keeps it as its own LUT level, the way
r12s0 pinned nets) and write fd_instr's D as
fd_redirect ? NOP : (hit ? c_data : alt_instr), which is one LUT4 per bit
with `hit` as a direct input (reset/kill stay on the flop SR pin, !hold on
CE). Do the same for fd_valid (hit | imem_ready), fd_pred_taken, fd_redirect
and fd_replay so each is a single LUT on `hit`. Also write the tag compare as
~|(rd_tag[9:0] ^ pc[19:10]) ANDed with the early (!sweeping & in_range &
valid-bit) term so it is a LUT4/LUT4 tree rather than an 8-cell ALU carry
chain (2 levels vs ~3.8 ns of chain entry/exit nets).

title: Validity-qualified F/D: take cache-hit compare out of the 32-bit F/D instruction capture (hit-free, reset-free fd_instr; ID/EX ctrl gated by fd_valid)
motivation:
The r13s2 champion (244.35, Fmax 91.752 MHz, cycles 3,755,007) reports its worst path as
cpu/u_if/fpc_4 -> cpu/u_if/u_ic -> cpu/u_if -> fd_instr_6, 17 cells, 18.2 ns. That is not the
fpc loop any more (which r13s2 made tag-free); it is the F/D instruction DATA capture:
    fd_instr <= (reset|kill|fd_redirect) ? NOP : hit ? c_data : (imem_ready ? imem_data : NOP)
`hit` is fpc -> tag RAM16 -> 4-level MUX2_LUT read -> 10-bit compare (3 LUT levels) ->
AND(valid, in_range, !sweeping) -> fan-out 32 -> data mux, i.e. the longest chain in the core
sits in front of 32 data flops that only exist to carry bits. The data bits themselves (RAM read,
4 mux levels) arrive 3-4 cells earlier than `hit`. Only the 1-bit control flops (fd_valid,
fd_pred_taken, fd_redirect, fd_replay, RAS enables) genuinely need `hit`. The remaining critical
groups (ID cones, regfile/BSRAM -> u_id, forward -> ALU) sit at ~16 ns, so removing the 17-cell
front-end path is worth up to ~10% Fmax if nothing else is added to it. This is a structural
change to what the F/D register means (a register that carries a payload plus a validity bit,
instead of a payload that is forced into a NOP encoding), not another predictor or cache resize,
and it follows the lesson from r4s1/r5s1 that data flops must not see reset/bubble/late-select
terms: only ctrl/valid flops do.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make F/D a validity-qualified register and keep every late/tag-dependent term off its 32-bit
instruction data path.

1. if_stage.sv: fd_instr (and fd_pc/fd_pred_target/fd_bht_cnt, already reset-free) becomes a pure
   data flop with clock enable only:
       if (!hold) fd_instr <= imem_ready ? imem_data : c_data;
   No reset, no kill, no fd_redirect, no `hit`, no NOP constant. Per bit this is one LUT4
   (hold, imem_ready, imem_data bit, RAM-mux output) and the RAM read arrives as the last LUT
   input. The bus word wins whenever the bus delivered (it is the authoritative word, equal to
   the cached copy on a hit; formal/cosim already tolerate stale-on-hit because the cache is
   never snooped), and when the bus did not deliver the slot is either a hit (c_data is
   correct) or a miss/replay slot (fd_valid = 0, c_data is garbage that must be harmless).
   The control flops are unchanged: fd_valid <= slot_ok, fd_pred_taken, fd_redirect, fd_replay
   keep `hit` at their D pins (4 fan-out instead of 32+), and `reset | kill` still clear fd_valid.
2. id_stage.sv: since a bubble slot no longer carries the NOP encoding, gate the decoded control
   bundle by the slot's validity at the ID/EX capture:
       reg_q.ctrl <= in.valid ? ctrl_decoded : '0;
   (ID/EX valid is already captured from in.valid.) With ctrl = 0 the garbage slot has
   reg_write = mem_read = mem_write = is_branch = is_jump = 0, so it cannot write the regfile or
   dmem, cannot be forwarded from (forward_unit gates on id_ex/EX-MEM reg_write), cannot mispredict
   and cannot raise a trap; rs/rd/imm/op_a/op_b payload bits of a bubble are never consumed.
   Check every consumer of ID/EX.ctrl for the bubble case (hazard_unit load-use uses
   id_ex_mem_read of the instruction in EX, which is now 0 for a bubble; ex_stage is_mdu already
   includes in.valid; bht_upd_valid includes in.valid).
3. core.sv / hazard_unit.sv: the regfile read addresses and hazard/forward compares keep reading
   the F/D instruction bits. A garbage instruction in an invalid slot may add a spurious 1-cycle
   load-use stall when it follows a load (performance only, never a correctness issue: stall_id
   holds ID/EX and the bubble slot is simply re-presented). Leave the port list of hazard_unit
   and forward_unit untouched (test_*.py drive them); if a cheap valid gate is wanted it must be
   done in core.sv by gating the compare inputs, not by adding ports.
4. branch_predictor.sv / icache.sv: unchanged except that nothing may use fd_instr as a NOP
   marker. The RAS fire/push/pop terms, hint, BHT, tag/data/hint arrays (flat async-read
   distributed RAM), reset sweep, fd_redirect/fd_replay repair and EX kill_q recovery stay
   exactly as in r13s2, so the formal memory structure that passed (and that r12s1/r12s2 broke)
   is identical and no new memory or wide state is added (fewer flops: ~32 data flops lose their
   reset/clear mux).

Expected effect: cycles identical to r13s2 within noise (bubble semantics unchanged; at worst a
handful of spurious load-use stalls on replay slots, <0.1%). The 17-cell fpc -> hit -> fd_instr
path disappears; the new worst front-end path is fpc -> tag -> hit -> 1-bit control flops
(~10-11 cells, ~12-13 ns), well under the ~16 ns ID/EX cones, so Fmax should rise to the
place-and-route ceiling of those cones (~97-100 MHz median) from 91.75, i.e. ~+6-8% fitness.
Risk: the gain is capped by the other ~16 ns groups and by the ~10% seed spread; the correctness
risk is a bubble slot leaking a side effect, which the formal suite (unique/causal/ill/liveness)
and cosim cover directly. Run only causal_ch0 and one insn_* check first to confirm formal time is
unchanged (it should be: no new memory).

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-002-r14s1 (improvement, +9.42%): Making the 32-bit `fd_instr` capture a pure data flop (`imem_ready ? imem_data : c_data`, CE only, no reset/kill/NOP, no cache `hit`) and moving "bubble" semantics to the 1-bit side (`fd_valid` kept on `hit`, `reg_q.ctrl <= in.valid ? ctrl_decoded : '0` at ID/EX) scored 267.36 vs the 244.35 r13s2 champion (+9.4%, above the +6% estimate) with identical memory structure, so the 17-cell fpc -> tag RAM -> compare -> `hit` -> fan-out-32 data-mux path was the real limiter and the lever was deleting the late signal from the wide datapath, not reordering it (sibling r14s0, which kept `hit` as a last-LUT select, got +5.8%) — carry a payload plus a validity bit and gate the side effects (ctrl/reg_write/mem/branch) at the consumer's 1-bit capture instead of forcing a NOP encoding into wide data flops, and expect the next limiter to be the ~16 ns ID/EX and forward -> ALU cones.

title: Miss-time F/D taken-CTI repair: use the registered fill-time predecode of the bus word to redirect cold-line JAL/branches one cycle later instead of a 3-cycle EX mispredict
motivation:
The r13s2 tag-free front end predicts only from the cache line's stored
fill-time hint, which is tag-independent and therefore meaningless when the
fetch misses. A direct-mapped 256 x 1-word I-cache (1 KiB) is far smaller
than CoreMark's hot code footprint, so a sizeable share of fetches are
misses, and every taken JAL or taken branch (BHT MSB set) fetched on a miss
slot is currently carried with pred_taken = 0. EX then finds
"taken but not predicted" and takes the full registered-kill recovery
(branch in EX -> kill_q -> fpc <= kill_target -> refetch -> F/D -> ID: a
3-cycle penalty), even though the bus word, its predecode (f_always / f_br /
18-bit static target) and the BHT counter (tag-free, indexed by pc) were all
in hand in the miss cycle, because the same predecode is already computed
for the cache write port. Past lessons say direction/indirect/recovery
predictors are at the noise floor on hit-path state; this targets a distinct
class the tag-free redesign introduced: CTIs on cold or conflict-evicted
lines, which the old bus-word predecode (r6-r10 era) predicted at fetch.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Capture the miss-time predecode in the F/D stage and repair from flops one
cycle later, reusing the existing fd_redirect / squash machinery. Only
if_stage.sv changes; branch_predictor.sv already exports f_always, f_br,
f_tgt and bht_cnt for the fetch pc.

In the fetch cycle (miss with the bus delivering, i.e. !hit && imem_ready):
  rep = f_always | (f_br & bht_cnt[1])
This ends at flop D pins only, exactly like the existing
fd_redirect <= !hit && (spec_taken || !imem_ready) term (hit is already
there, so no new late-signal fan-out into the fpc loop). New F/D state:
  fd_rep       <= !hit && imem_ready && rep          (1 flop)
  fd_rep_tgt   <= f_tgt                              (18 data flops, !hold)
and the existing flops become
  fd_pred_taken <= (hit && spec_taken) | (!hit && imem_ready && rep)
  fd_redirect   <= !hit && (spec_taken || !imem_ready || rep)
so the slot enters ID/EX with pred_taken = 1 and EX verifies it as for any
predicted-taken branch/JAL (direction check only; the BHT update keeps
using the counter carried from fetch, which is correct for a miss because
the BHT has no tag). In the next cycle (all flop-sourced, no tag compare, no
bus) the early next-fpc select becomes
  early_pc = fd_redirect ? (fd_rep ? fd_rep_tgt
                                   : (fd_replay ? fd_pc : fd_pc + 1))
                         : fpc + 1
The slot fetched in that cycle is wrong-path / bogus-hint and is squashed by
the existing fd_redirect branch (F/D <= NOP bubble, fire = 0 so the RAS is
not polluted). The fetch at the correct target happens the cycle after, so
a miss-slot taken CTI costs 1 bubble instead of 3 (saving 2 cycles each);
a not-taken branch or a no-BHT-vote branch behaves exactly as now. RAS
push/pop for the miss slot is already correct (ras_call / ras_ret use the
bus-word predecode when bus_ok). `ret` is not repaired (its RAS entry has
already been popped); JALR and misaligned / out-of-range targets stay
f_*=0, so those keep going through the EX path unchanged. Hold/kill
behaviour follows the fd_redirect precedent: kill clears fd_rep with
fd_redirect, and a held F/D keeps its flags until !hold.

Cost: 19 flops, one 2:1 18-bit mux in the early (flop-sourced) part of
next_fpc, two extra OR terms on existing flop D pins. No new memory, no
change to the fetch loop's late terms (spec_taken / hit), so Fmax should
stay at the r13s2 level (~91.7 MHz median) and the gain is pure cycles. The
gain scales with (miss rate x taken-CTI density x 2 cycles); a few percent
of CoreMark cycles is plausible but I did not measure the miss rate, hence
low-to-medium confidence. Suggested check before the full flow: add a
temporary counter of repaired slots in simulation to confirm the repair
fires on the order of 50-100K times per 10 iterations.

Add fd_rep / fd_rep_tgt[19:2] F/D flops loaded from the fetch-cycle miss predecode (f_always | f_br & bht_cnt[1], gated by !hit && imem_ready, tgt = f_tgt); OR the repair term into fd_pred_taken and fd_redirect; extend the early_pc select so a pending repair loads {12'b0, fd_rep_tgt} instead of fd_pc / fd_pc+1; clear fd_rep on reset/kill and on the squash branch.

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-003-r14s2 (regression, -5.79%): Repairing miss-slot taken JAL/branches one cycle later from a bus-word predecode (`miss_rep` = `imem_ready && (f_always || f_br && bht_cnt[1])` into `fd_pred_taken`/`fd_redirect`/`fd_rep`, 18 `fd_rep_tgt` flops, an extra `fd_rep` leg in the flop-sourced `early_pc` mux) scored 230.19 vs the 244.35 r13s2 base against a +3% (low-confidence) cycle ceiling, so since fitness ≈ Fmax/cycles the loss is almost certainly Fmax, from re-attaching the late `imem_data` -> predecode -> static-target adder/compare cone to several flop D pins that r13s2 had cleared of bus-derived logic — "ends only at D pins" does not make a bus-word predecode free when it adds fan-out and a wide adder on the bus path, so a fetch-miss repair needs a measured miss-slot-CTI count and a `make timing` check of the `imem_data` paths first, and the cheaper variant is to take the 2-cycle saving from the already-registered fill-time hint at the next stage rather than re-decoding the bus word in the fetch cycle.

title: Cut the two tied 16.3 ns routing-bound cones: low-fanout fpc replicas for tag/hint RAM reads + raw tag-eq into the last LUT of the fd_* flops + per-lane regfile read decode
motivation:
`make timing` on the r14s1 champion (place option 0, 90.459 MHz) shows two groups tied at the
top of the setup report, so cutting only one of them cannot move the median:
  (1) cpu/u_if/fpc_3 -> u_ic tag/hint RAM -> tag-eq carry chain -> n443_s3 (hit, fanout 4)
      -> n443_s2 -> fd_replay / fd_redirect / fd_pred_taken / fd_valid D: 16.349 ns arrival
      (data path 11.02 ns), 15 cells.
  (2) cpu/u_if/fd_instr_24 -> u_id regfile read decode (LUT fanout 8 -> LUT fanout 32)
      -> 5-LUT read-mux chain -> rs2_val_16 D: 16.344 ns, 8 cells.
Both are routing-bound, not logic-bound: path 1 is 8.0 ns route vs 2.8 ns cell delay, with
fpc_3 Q at fanout 296 (2.18 ns net into the RAM16 address pin) and three 1.4-1.5 ns hops
RAM->mux, tag-eq->hit, hit->control LUT; path 2 has a fanout-32 decode net of 3.16 ns.
Earlier iterations (r12s0 select-net replication +4%, r14s0 last-LUT late select +5.8%,
r14s1 deleting the late term +9.4%) each fixed one such cone and each was worth a few percent,
but they were never applied together on a base where these two are the only limiters.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three local netlist-structure edits, all cycle-neutral, same memories, same function.

A. Fetch-address replicas (if_stage.sv, icache.sv, branch_predictor.sv).
   Add two copies of fpc[19:2] loaded with identical D/CE/reset as fpc: `fpc_tag`
   (drives only the tag RAM read address and the tag-equality operand pc[19:10]) and
   `fpc_hint` (drives the hint RAM read address and the BHT read index). Mark them
   `(* syn_preserve *)` / `syn_keep` so Gowin does not merge them back. The original fpc keeps
   the data-array read (not timing critical), imem_addr, fpc+1, fd_pc, the fill/write
   address and in_range. fpc_3 fanout drops from ~296 to ~130, the tag and hint RAM address
   nets go from one die-wide fanout to two ~50-100 fanout nets placed next to their RAMs.
   Cost ~36 flops. icache gets an extra read-address port (`pc_t`, `pc_h`); BHT read uses `pc_h`.
B. Raw tag equality straight into the final LUT4 of the four F/D control flops (if_stage.sv,
   icache.sv). In the report `hit` is built as eq -> n443_s3 (fanout 4) -> per-flop LUT; the
   intermediate hit LUT costs a 1.4-1.5 ns hop plus 0.37 ns. Export from icache
   `tag_eq` (10-bit equality only), `tag_vh = rd_tag[10] & !sweeping & in_range` (early
   except for the RAM valid bit, ready before the compare), and write
     clr  = reset | kill
     adv  = !clr & !hold & !fd_redirect          keep = !clr & hold
     fd_valid_d      = keep&fd_valid      | adv&imem_ready | (adv&tag_vh) & tag_eq
     fd_replay_d     = keep&fd_replay     | adv&!imem_ready & !(tag_vh & tag_eq)
     fd_pred_taken_d = keep&fd_pred_taken | (adv&tag_vh&spec_taken) & tag_eq
     fd_redirect_d   = keep&fd_redirect   | (adv&(spec_taken|!imem_ready)) & !(tag_vh & tag_eq)
   i.e. D = A | (B & tag_eq) or A | (C & !(tag_vh & tag_eq)): at most four inputs, so
   the carry-chain/LUT equality output feeds one LUT4 per flop and `hit` as a shared signal
   is no longer on the path. `syn_keep` on A/B/C so the mapper cannot re-chain them behind
   the compare. `hit` remains defined (tag_vh & tag_eq) for any non-critical user.
C. Per-lane regfile read decode (reg_file.sv only; port list unchanged because
   test_reg_file.py drives it). Compute the 5->one-hot read-address predecode once per
   byte lane (4 copies per read port, `syn_keep`) so each decode net has fanout 8 instead
   of 32 and is placed with its byte slice of the 31x32 register flops, instead of a
   single decode spanning the die (3.16 ns net in path 2). The bypass flags rs*_byp and the
   read data are unchanged.
Expected effect: path 1 loses ~1 ns of address-net delay and ~1.8 ns of hit LUT + hop;
path 2 loses ~1-1.5 ns of fanout-32 net. Because both limiters must drop together, the
realised gain depends on the next tier (~15-16 ns forward -> ALU cones); estimate +5-7%

title: Defer I-cache tag compare into the F/D stage (registered tag, comb hit_q) and spend the freed fetch slack on a 512-line cache
motivation:
The champion's limiting group in the last make-timing report is still the fetch cone
`fpc -> tag LUT-RAM read -> 10-bit compare -> hit -> slot_ok -> fd_replay / fd_redirect /
fd_valid / fd_pred_taken` (15 cells, 16.35 ns, r14s1; 17 cells in r13s2, 11 cells in r14s2).
r14s1 already took `hit` out of the 32-bit instruction capture; what is left is that the tag
RAM read and the 10-bit compare are chained inside ONE cycle only to produce four 1-bit flags
that are consumed one cycle later anyway (fd_replay / fd_redirect steer fpc from flops in the
next cycle; fd_valid / fd_pred_taken only matter to ID). That serialisation is purely
structural: the compare can be done at the start of the F/D cycle from registered tag bits at
the same architectural cycle count. Because the tag compare then no longer shares a cycle with
the RAM read, the cache can also grow: the CoreMark 2K hot code (list find/sort, state machine,
crc, matrix kernels) is larger than the 1 KiB 256-line cache, and every miss that coincides
with a not-ready bus (~22%) costs a replay cycle. Prior I-cache work (r11s1, r13s2, r14s1) is
the only front-end line that has paid; the remaining untested axis is balancing the loop
across the F/D flop boundary instead of removing logic from it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
(1) Deferred hit. icache.sv stops producing `hit`. It exports the raw tag read as flop-ready
bits: tag_ok = !sweeping && rd_tag[valid] && in_range (in_range and sweeping are already
early flop/pc terms) and tag_lo = rd_tag[tag bits]. if_stage.sv registers fd_tag_ok and fd_tag
(CE = !hold, no reset, same enable as fd_instr/fd_pc), plus fd_bus (= imem_ready at fetch) and
fd_spec (= spec_taken at fetch) and a 1-bit fd_squash (the slot fetched while the previous
slot's redirect/replay was active). In the F/D cycle everything is derived from flops:
  hit_q       = fd_tag_ok && (fd_tag == fd_pc[tag range])          (~3 LUT levels)
  fd_valid    = !fd_squash && (fd_bus || hit_q)
  fd_replay   = !fd_squash && !(fd_bus || hit_q)
  fd_redirect = !fd_squash && !hit_q && (fd_spec || !fd_bus)
  fd_pred_taken = !fd_squash && hit_q && fd_spec
fd_squash <= fd_redirect (when !hold) and is SET by kill/reset (a killed/reset F/D slot is a
bubble, as fd_valid <= 0 is today), which reproduces the existing
squash-the-slot-fetched-during-a-redirect behaviour at the identical cycle count. The new
flop->compare->{early_pc/sel_spec mux, F/D flags, RAS fire, id_stage valid gating} paths are
~6-7 cells, and the fpc -> RAM read -> flop paths are ~5, so the 15-cell fpc->hit->flag cone
disappears. id_stage.sv needs no change (`in.valid` / `in.pred_taken` just come out of a few
LUTs instead of a flop; ID/EX ctrl gating and pred_taken capture end at D pins). Sweep,
fill-every-bus-cycle semantic, hint RAM read in the fpc loop and RAS are untouched.
(2) Use the slack: double the cache to 512 lines (index pc[10:2], tag {valid, pc[19:11]},
9-bit compare, 512-cycle reset sweep which still ends far before the CoreMark start marker).
The only longer paths are one extra MUX2 level on the RAM read (hint read -> spec_taken ->
next_fpc loop, tag read -> flop); the BHT stays 256 x 2b indexed by pc[9:2]. Cost ~+1.2K LUT
(LUT-RAM), well inside the 20K-LUT part. Expected: removal of the top fetch cone gives a few
percent Fmax (the next limiters, BSRAM->u_mem->u_id and regfile->u_id, sit ~0.5 ns lower), and
the doubled capacity trims miss-and-bus-stall replays for ~3-4% fewer cycles. If the
512-line growth shows up as the new limiter it can be reverted to 256 lines without touching
the deferred-hit structure (the two are independent parameters in icache.sv).

Add F/D flops fd_tag_ok, fd_tag, fd_bus, fd_spec, fd_squash (CE = !hold; kill/reset set fd_squash so the slot is a bubble). Derive hit_q / fd_valid / fd_replay / fd_redirect / fd_pred_taken combinationally from those flops and fd_pc; use them in early_pc / sel_spec / fire / out.valid / out.pred_taken. fd_squash <= fd_redirect reproduces the existing squash of the slot fetched during a redirect. fd_instr capture (imem_ready ? imem_data : c_data), fpc CE and the hint-driven next_fpc loop stay as in r14s1.

lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-002-r15s1 (regression, -3.57%): Registering the raw tag read (`fd_tag_ok`/`fd_tag`, plus `fd_bus`/`fd_spec`/`fd_squash`) so the 9-bit compare runs from flops in the F/D cycle, and doubling the I-cache to 512 lines, scored 257.81 vs the 267.36 r14s1 champion at the same cycle count instead of the +6% estimated, so moving the compare behind the F/D flops did not delete the fpc -> RAM read -> `hit` -> flag cone, it relocated it — `fd_valid`/`fd_replay`/`fd_redirect`/`fd_pred_taken` went from flop outputs (which r14s1 had made the clean carriers of validity into ID/EX ctrl) to ~3-LUT functions on the `early_pc`/`sel_spec` mux and ID valid-gating cones that already sit at ~16 ns, and the 512-line MUX2 level on the hint/tag read is a second unmeasured cost (the two edits were bundled, so which dominated is unproven, and -3.6% is also inside the ~10% seed spread) — keep every flag that ID and the fpc loop consume as a flop output, and retry cache growth (index/tag width alone) as a separate single-edit run backed by a `make timing` fpc-loop check.

title: F/D-stage taken-CTI repair for I-cache miss slots from the registered fill-time predecode
motivation:
The fetch-time predictor (tag-independent hint RAM + BHT) only predicts a taken
JAL/branch when the I-cache line for the fetch pc is present. On a miss slot the
hint belongs to another pc: a bogus "taken" hint costs a 1-cycle alias-fix bubble,
and a really-taken JAL/branch whose line missed gets pred_taken=0 and is only
caught by the EX mispredict check (registered kill_q, 3-cycle penalty). The 1 KiB
direct-mapped cache misses a few tens of percent of fetches on CoreMark, so a
meaningful share of taken CTIs fall into miss slots. r14s2 tried to repair these
by re-predecoding the bus word in the fetch cycle and attaching it to several flop
D pins; it lost 5.8% to Fmax, and its lesson names the cheap variant: take the
saving from the already-computed fill-time predecode, registered, at the next stage.
Fmax is plateaued at ~100 MHz (ID/EX and BSRAM->u_id cones tie the fetch tag path),
so the only remaining predictor lever is cycles, and it must not touch any
imem_data-derived cone.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Register the fill-time predecode that branch_predictor already computes for the
cache write port (f_always, f_br, f_tgt[19:2]; no new logic, only a second load on
those nets) into 20 F/D data flops (CE = !hold, no reset), together with a 1-bit
fd_fill flag "this slot's word came from the bus on a miss" (!hit && imem_ready,
the same kind of 1-bit term fd_redirect already has). In the F/D cycle everything
is flop-sourced:
  late_taken = fd_fill && (fd_f_always || (fd_f_br && fd_bht_cnt[1]))
(fd_bht_cnt is already carried; the BHT is tagless so it is valid for a miss).
When late_taken is set, the slot is a valid instruction with a taken CTI whose
hint was wrong or absent: the slot fetched this cycle is squashed (merged into the
existing fd_redirect squash/`fire` handling as `redirect_now = fd_redirect ||
late_taken`), the next fpc is fd_f_tgt (one extra flop-sourced leg in the early_pc
mux, below kill and above fd_pc+1), and the slot reaches ID with pred_taken = 1 and
pred_target = fd_f_tgt via a flop-only override in the if_stage output
(out.pred_taken = fd_pred_taken | late_taken; out.pred_target = late_taken ?
fd_f_tgt : fd_pred_target) so EX verifies it exactly like a normal prediction
(static targets are word-aligned and in the low 1 MiB by the predecode's
static_ok, so the existing misalign/trap and RAS logic is unaffected; `ret` is not
repaired). A taken JAL/branch in a miss slot then costs 1 bubble instead of 3
(mispredict) and a bogus-hint alias fix that was really taken costs 1 instead of
1 plus a later 3. The BHT update, EX mispredict check, kill_q recovery, cache
fill and RAS push/pop are unchanged. No imem_data-derived signal reaches any new
flop D pin through new logic (the f_* nets already exist for the cache hint write),
no tag compare reaches the fpc loop, and the new decision logic is two LUTs from
flops, so the Fmax risk that sank r14s2 is avoided. Expected: ~2-4% fewer cycles at
unchanged Fmax; ~+20 FF, ~+40 LUT.

implementation_notes:
# r15s2 implementation notes: F/D-stage taken-CTI repair for I-cache miss slots

## What changed (cores/bench/rtl/if_stage.sv only)

- New F/D data flops (CE = !hold, no reset): `fd_f_always`, `fd_f_br`,
  `fd_f_tgt[19:2]`, loaded straight from the existing `f_always` / `f_br` /
  `f_tgt` predecode nets of `branch_predictor` (the nets that already feed the
  cache hint write port). No new logic on any `imem_data`-derived net, only a
  second load.
- New 1-bit control flop `fd_fill <= !hit && imem_ready` (the slot's word came
  from the bus on a miss), in the same reset/kill/squash block as
  `fd_valid`/`fd_redirect`/`fd_replay`; cleared on reset, kill and when the slot
  fetched this cycle is squashed.
- `late_taken = fd_fill && (fd_f_always || (fd_f_br && fd_bht_cnt[1]))`, a pure
  function of four flops. `redirect_now = fd_redirect || late_taken`.
  - squashes the slot fetched this cycle (F/D control next-state, and `fire`,
    which gates the RAS push/pop, so a squashed slot does not touch the RAS);
  - `early_pc`: kill > late_taken ? `{12'b0, fd_f_tgt}` > fd_redirect ?
    (fd_replay ? fd_pc : fd_pc+1) > fpc+1; `sel_spec` also masked by `late_taken`;
  - output override: `out.pred_taken = fd_pred_taken | late_taken`,
    `out.pred_target = late_taken ? {12'b0, fd_f_tgt} : fd_pred_target`. EX then
    verifies it as an ordinary prediction (BHT update, mispredict check, kill_q
    recovery unchanged).
- `branch_predictor.sv`, `icache.sv`, EX and the rest are untouched.

`fd_fill` implies `fd_valid` and excludes `fd_replay`/`fd_pred_taken` (all three
derive from `hit`/`imem_ready` in the same cycle), so `late_taken` never fires on
a bubble or a replay slot and the OR in `out.pred_taken` is exact. The static
target comes from the same bus word / fpc as `fd_instr`, and `static_ok` already
restricts it to word-aligned targets in the low 1 MiB, so the EX misalign/trap and
RAS logic is unaffected. `ret` is not repaired.

## Deviations
None from the hypothesis plan.

## Measured effect (local, `--istall --dstall` CoreMark, Verilator)
Bracketed CoreMark cycles: baseline 3,754,779 -> 3,743,682 (-11,097, **-0.30 %**).
This is well below the hypothesis' 2-4 % estimate. Counters over ~3.7 M cycles:
~152 K miss slots delivered by the bus, only ~12.8 K of them are late-taken CTIs
(10.4 K branches, 2.4 K JALs; 7.6 K of them also had a bogus taken hint, i.e. were
alias-fixed before), against ~45.6 K EX mispredicts in total. A JAL-only variant
saves just 4.7 K cycles; the branch leg (BHT-gated) adds the rest. So the cycle
ceiling of this idea on CoreMark is ~0.3-0.5 %, and it only pays if Fmax is
unchanged (+~22 FF, ~+10-20 LUT; the f_* nets get one extra flop load each).

## Concerns
- Fmax: the f_always/f_br/f_tgt nets (imem_data -> predecode -> 19-bit adder)
  now have a second sink (flop D pins) besides the hint-RAM write data; if the
  placer stretches that net the imem_data path could lengthen. No new logic was
  added on it. `late_taken` is 2 LUT levels from flops and joins `sel_spec` /
  `early_pc` / `fire`.
- A late-taken branch whose BHT counter says taken but actually falls through
  now costs 1 bubble + a 3-cycle recovery where the baseline cost 0; the net
  effect is still positive on CoreMark (measured above).

## Verification
- `verilator --lint-only -Wall -Wno-MULTITOP`: clean.
- Formal (`RTL_DIR=cores/bench/rtl CORE_NAME=bench WRAPPER=formal/wrapper_si.sv
  CHECKS_CFG=formal/checks_si.cfg bash formal/run_all.sh`; nret=1 wrapper): 53
  passed, 0 failed. (A first attempt reported failures only because a concurrent
  run's reaper deleted the shared riscv-formal work dir mid-run: `Can't open
  output file ../model/design.json`; no SBY check had failed. Re-run clean.)
- Cosim (`NRET=1 make cosim TARGET=bench`; plain `make cosim` builds with
  -DNRET=2 and fails on the `_1` ports for an nret=1 core): passed, 2 ELFs
  (selftest + CoreMark with and without stalls), CoreMark CRCs correct.

## Timing (single `make timing TARGET=bench` run, place option 0 only)
Fmax 94.78 MHz (champion median ~100.4 MHz over 3 placement options). Top paths:
`fpc -> icache tag RAM -> hit -> fd_redirect / fd_fill / fd_valid` (15.85 ns, the
pre-existing tag-compare-to-F/D-control cone; `fd_fill` is simply one more endpoint
of it, same D-pin structure as `fd_redirect`) and `fd_instr -> u_id` op_b/rs2_val
captures (15.84 ns, untouched by this change). No path through `late_taken`, the
new `fd_f_*` flops or the `imem_data` predecode appears in the top 5, so the
94.8 vs ~100 MHz gap is likely placement seed spread, but only one placement was
sampled here; the orchestrator's 3-option median is the real measure.
lesson: - 2026-10-03 hyp-20261003-003-r15s2 (regression, -3.31%): Registering the fill-time predecode (`fd_f_always`/`fd_f_br`/`fd_f_tgt`, 1-bit `fd_fill`) so `late_taken` is a flop-only function that squashes the slot, redirects `early_pc` and overrides `out.pred_taken`/`pred_target` scored 258.50 vs the 267.36 r14s1 champion, and the measured ceiling explains why it could not pay: only ~12.8K of ~152K miss-slot fetches are late-taken CTIs (10.4K branches, 2.4K JALs) against ~45.6K total EX mispredicts, so cycles fell just 0.30% (3,754,779 -> 3,743,682), not the 2-4% estimated, and any Fmax give-back above ~0.3% (the one sampled placement hit 94.8 MHz, with `fd_fill` added as another endpoint of the fpc -> tag RAM -> `hit` cone at 15.85 ns and `late_taken` joining `early_pc`/`sel_spec`/`fire`) turns it negative — miss-slot taken-CTI repair is exhausted on CoreMark, so count the affected-event ceiling from a Verilator counter before building any fetch-miss repair, and do not add terms to the fpc loop for a <1% cycle target.
